description: Maximize a selected-item numerator/denominator ratio subject to a minimum total denominator, using ratio bisection and a transformed 0/1 knapsack check.

source.discovery_note: OI Wiki article method description only; no text, examples, code, or tests reused.
source.method_reference: OI Wiki fractional-programming article: ratio bisection with transformed additive objective and denominator-constrained 0/1 knapsack feasibility.
source.license_note: OI Wiki states CC BY-SA 4.0 and SATA; only the algorithm idea is used.

output.meaning: floor(1000000 * maximum sum(a_i)/sum(b_i) among subsets with sum(b_i)>=W)

workspace.meaning: Two 33-entry i64 knapsack rows, bounded input item arrays, and fixed scalar bookkeeping.

contract.primary_method: Binary-search integer q in [0,1000000000] for the largest feasible threshold. Feasibility maximizes sum(1000000*a_i-q*b_i) over subsets with denominator sum at least W using two-row 0/1 knapsack DP over denominator sums capped at W; it is feasible iff the maximum is nonnegative.
contract.independent_method: Enumerate every nonempty subset, retain those whose denominator sum is at least W, compare exact ratios by integer cross-products, then floor the winning ratio multiplied by 1000000.
contract.complexity: Primary O(n*W*log(1000000001)) time and O(W) auxiliary space; independent O(2^n*n) time.
contract.invalid_cases: Null input, malformed length, out-of-bound n/W/a_i/b_i, or W greater than the total denominator returns -1.
contract.distinct_from: dinkelbach_fixed_cardinality_ratio selects exactly K items and iterates Dinkelbach updates using a top-K residual selector; this profile uses a minimum-denominator knapsack feasibility DP and ratio bisection.

generated_profile.description: Each feasible ratio is a denominator-weighted average of item ratios a_i/b_i<=1000, so the scaled result is at most 1000000000.
